page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with verse epigrams set in the same column. No margin notes. Running head at top, page number at top right, catchword at bottom right.

p.i: diolani superatos, cæsos, captos & ab Italia pulsos, inter pocula supra modum lætus ac ridens, spiritum effluisse dicitur, cum nec cœlum nec infernum post hanc vitam esse crederet. De hoc Leone Actius Sannazarius sic scribit:
Sacra sub extrema, si forte requiritis, hora / Cur Leo non poterat sumere? Vendiderat.
Pastor ut ambiguo Proteus dignoscitur ore, / Et dubius liquidis sæpe vagatur aquis:
Sic Leo nulla fides tibi, nec constantia rebus, / Factaq; promissa sunt odiosa tuis.
Nec bona, nec mala sunt dubio credenda Leoni, / Est etiam in verum ut vix adhibenda fides.
Quum ventrem imprudens avido natura Leoni / Fecisset, rimas præbuit huic geminas.
Non excrementis fuerat satis una: sed harum / Altera nunc clausa, nec minus illa vorat.
Gaude Roma, brevi hac solveris peste: fastidiet[?] / Alvum, tam magni ponderis impatiens.
Differat à Decimo quàm Iulius ipse Leone, / Discere ab amborum nomine Roma potest.
Iulius est hominis, bruti Leo. Iulius egit, / Quæ suasit ratio: quod libet, iste facit.
Nota hoc loco, quòd anno à Christi incarnatio-ne 261. quum Paulus Samosatenus in Ecclesia Chri

page.notes: Catchword "stiano" is printed in bold at the bottom right, under the last line. Long s is written as plain s throughout. Doubtful readings: "fastidiet" (the printed word is hard to read, marked [?]); "diolani" at the start of the page is printed as shown and may be a misprint for a place name, left as printed. The verse is set as one paragraph per couplet, lines joined by a space. Pencil or ink underlining under "cum nec cœlum nec infernum post hanc vitam esse crederet" and under "Nota hoc loco" and the dashes under the last lines are handwritten or marks, not print, and are not transcribed.
